--- title: "Hands-on Exercise 4c" subtitle: "Visualising Uncertainty" author: "Jedidiah Asaf T" format: html: toc: true code-fold: true --- ## Overview This hands-on exercise focuses on visualising uncertainty using error bars, confidence intervals, interactive charts, and uncertainty visualisation methods. ## Setup ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} if (!require(pacman)) install.packages("pacman") pacman::p_load( plotly, crosstalk, DT, ggdist, ggridges, colorspace, gganimate, tidyverse, knitr ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` The downloaded binary packages are in /var/folders/2p/h_606kv17738sdr7k_9l5vh00000gn/T//RtmpWOv0NI/downloaded_packages ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` The downloaded binary packages are in /var/folders/2p/h_606kv17738sdr7k_9l5vh00000gn/T//RtmpWOv0NI/downloaded_packages ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} exam <- read_csv("Exam_data.csv") ``` ::: ## Data Preview ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} glimpse(exam) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Rows: 322 Columns: 7 $ ID "Student321", "Student305", "Student289", "Student227", "Stude… $ CLASS "3I", "3I", "3H", "3F", "3I", "3I", "3I", "3I", "3I", "3H", "3… $ GENDER "Male", "Female", "Male", "Male", "Male", "Female", "Male", "M… $ RACE "Malay", "Malay", "Chinese", "Chinese", "Malay", "Malay", "Chi… $ ENGLISH 21, 24, 26, 27, 27, 31, 31, 31, 33, 34, 34, 36, 36, 36, 37, 38… $ MATHS 9, 22, 16, 77, 11, 16, 21, 18, 19, 49, 39, 35, 23, 36, 49, 30,… $ SCIENCE 15, 16, 16, 31, 25, 16, 25, 27, 15, 37, 42, 22, 32, 36, 35, 45… ``` ::: ::: # 1. Summary Statistics ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} my_sum <- exam %>% group_by(RACE) %>% summarise( n = n(), mean = mean(MATHS, na.rm = TRUE), sd = sd(MATHS, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop" ) %>% mutate( se = sd / sqrt(n - 1) ) knitr::kable(my_sum, format = "html", digits = 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
RACE n mean sd se
Chinese 193 76.51 15.69 1.13
Indian 12 60.67 23.35 7.04
Malay 108 57.44 21.13 2.04
Others 9 69.67 10.72 3.79
````` ::: ::: # 2. Visualising Uncertainty with Error Bars ## 2.1 Standard Error Bars ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(my_sum) + geom_errorbar( aes( x = RACE, ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se ), width = 0.2, colour = "black", alpha = 0.9, linewidth = 0.5 ) + geom_point( aes( x = RACE, y = mean ), stat = "identity", color = "red", size = 1.5, alpha = 1 ) + labs( title = "Standard Error of Mean Maths Score by Race", x = "Race", y = "Mean Maths score" ) + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](hands_on_exercise_4c_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## 2.2 95% Confidence Interval ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(my_sum) + geom_errorbar( aes( x = reorder(RACE, -mean), ymin = mean - 1.96 * se, ymax = mean + 1.96 * se ), width = 0.2, colour = "black", alpha = 0.9, linewidth = 0.5 ) + geom_point( aes( x = reorder(RACE, -mean), y = mean ), stat = "identity", color = "red", size = 1.5, alpha = 1 ) + labs( title = "95% Confidence Interval of Mean Maths Score by Race", x = "Race", y = "Mean Maths score" ) + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](hands_on_exercise_4c_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: # 3. Interactive Error Bars ## 3.1 99% Confidence Interval with Linked Table ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} shared_df <- SharedData$new(my_sum) p <- ggplot(shared_df) + geom_errorbar( aes( x = reorder(RACE, -mean), ymin = mean - 2.58 * se, ymax = mean + 2.58 * se ), width = 0.2, colour = "black", alpha = 0.9, linewidth = 0.5 ) + geom_point( aes( x = RACE, y = mean, text = paste( "Race:", RACE, "
N:", n, "
Average score:", round(mean, 2), "
99% CI: [", round(mean - 2.58 * se, 2), ",", round(mean + 2.58 * se, 2), "]" ) ), stat = "identity", color = "red", size = 1.5, alpha = 1 ) + xlab("Race") + ylab("Average Maths Score") + ggtitle("99% Confidence Interval of Average Maths Scores by Race") + theme_minimal() + theme( axis.text.x = element_text( angle = 45, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1 ) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning in geom_point(aes(x = RACE, y = mean, text = paste("Race:", RACE, : Ignoring unknown aesthetics: text ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} bscols( widths = c(6, 6), ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text"), DT::datatable( shared_df, rownames = FALSE, class = "compact", width = "100%", options = list( pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE ) ) %>% formatRound( columns = c("mean", "sd", "se"), digits = 2 ) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: # 4. Visualising Uncertainty with ggdist ## 4.1 Mean Point Interval Plot ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} exam %>% ggplot( aes( x = RACE, y = MATHS ) ) + stat_pointinterval() + labs( title = "Visualising Confidence Intervals of Mean Maths Score", subtitle = "Mean point + multiple interval plot", x = "Race", y = "Maths score" ) + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](hands_on_exercise_4c_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## 4.2 Median Point Interval Plot ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} exam %>% ggplot( aes( x = RACE, y = MATHS ) ) + stat_pointinterval( .width = 0.95, .point = median, .interval = qi ) + labs( title = "Visualising Confidence Intervals of Median Maths Score", subtitle = "Median point + interval plot", x = "Race", y = "Maths score" ) + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning in layer_slabinterval(data = data, mapping = mapping, stat = StatPointinterval, : Ignoring unknown parameters: `.point` and `.interval` ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](hands_on_exercise_4c_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## 4.3 Multiple Interval Plot ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} exam %>% ggplot( aes( x = RACE, y = MATHS ) ) + stat_pointinterval( .width = c(0.95, 0.99), show.legend = TRUE ) + labs( title = "Visualising 95% and 99% Intervals of Mean Maths Score", subtitle = "Mean point + multiple interval plot", x = "Race", y = "Maths score" ) + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](hands_on_exercise_4c_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-9-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## 4.4 Gradient Interval Plot ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} exam %>% ggplot( aes( x = RACE, y = MATHS ) ) + stat_gradientinterval( fill = "skyblue", show.legend = TRUE ) + labs( title = "Visualising Confidence Intervals of Mean Maths Score", subtitle = "Gradient + interval plot", x = "Race", y = "Maths score" ) + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](hands_on_exercise_4c_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: # 5. Optional: Hypothetical Outcome Plot This section is optional because the `ungeviz` package may need to be installed from GitHub. To avoid rendering errors, the code is shown but not executed. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # install.packages("devtools") # devtools::install_github("wilkelab/ungeviz") library(ungeviz) ggplot( data = exam, aes( x = factor(RACE), y = MATHS ) ) + geom_point( position = position_jitter( height = 0.3, width = 0.05 ), size = 0.4, color = "#0072B2", alpha = 1 / 2 ) + geom_hpline( data = sampler(25, group = RACE), height = 0.6, color = "#D55E00" ) + theme_bw() + transition_states(.draw, 1, 3) ``` ::: ## Learning Reflection In this exercise, I learned that uncertainty should not be hidden in visual analytics. Error bars, confidence intervals, and interval plots help communicate how reliable or uncertain a point estimate is. Interactive visualisation also helps users inspect the uncertainty values more clearly.
